rationale: The two most strongly separated landmarker tails are homophily_violation (p99=0.848, p95=0.738, mean=0.379) and local_affinity (p99=0.826, p95=0.725, mean=0.338), and both are grounded in the profile's homophily=0.643, which is high enough for neighbor-agreement to be meaningful but far from perfect, leaving room for feature-neighbor mismatch to flag anomalies. These form the dominant local view; they share a mechanism family, so I add complementary rather than redundant signals. attr_struct_mismatch supplies a cross-modal view (clean tail p99=0.60 vs mean=0.148) motivated by the strongly heterogeneous structure (is_power_law=true, max_degree=2556, degree_std=54.82) that makes attribute-based and structure-based rankings likely to diverge for hub/fringe nodes. spectral adds an orthogonal high-frequency view (p99=0.476 vs mean=0.093); the tiny spectral_gap=0.113 and clustering_coeff=0.0 mean signals are poorly smoothed, so localized high-frequency responses should stand out. I exclude density (landmarker is effectively dead: p50=p90=0.0, mean=0.0047, consistent with clustering_coeff=0.0 collapsing local embedding density) and community (nearly flat: p90=0.217 barely above p50=0.178 despite modularity=0.4746, so modularity residual adds little discriminative separation).

The label-free landmarkers give the clearest evidence. local_affinity has the best-separated upper tail (p90 0.665, p95 0.725, p99 0.826) and is directly supported by homophily 0.6427: neighbors mostly agree, so the minority of low-affinity nodes stand out sharply. homophily_violation shows an almost identical tail (p95 0.738, p99 0.848) but is the same feature-neighbor-mismatch mechanism, so I take only one of the pair to avoid redundancy and spend the other slots on complementary views. attr_struct_mismatch is a genuinely different (cross-modal) signal and still shows a real tail (p95 0.440, p99 0.602) over feature_dim 64, catching nodes where attribute and structure rankings diverge rather than just local disagreement. community adds a structural view: modularity 0.4746 with 18 communities is meaningful clustering, and its landmarker is flat through p95 (0.229) then jumps at p99 (0.639), i.e. a rare set of nodes that adhere to no community, which is exactly the anomaly regime. reconstruction is added as a robust joint attribute+structure anchor (DOMINANT-style) on dense features (feature_sparsity 0.0), complementing the three targeted views. I drop density (landmarker essentially flat, p90 0.0, p95 0.006, and clustering_coeff 0.0 means no local neighborhood structure for LOF/kNN to exploit) and spectral (only a modest tail, p99 0.476, and the power-law degree with degree_std 54.82 / max_degree 2556 would confound high-frequency response with hubness).

The landmarker distributions show two paradigms with a strongly separated upper tail: local_affinity (p90 0.665, p99 0.826, std 0.253) and homophily_violation (p90 0.677, p99 0.848). Both are neighbor-feature-agreement views and are mutually redundant, so I keep only local_affinity as the primary signal; it is well founded because homophily = 0.643 (>= 0.3) means neighbors genuinely agree in normal regions, making low-agreement nodes informative. For complementarity I add attr_struct_mismatch, which has its own real (if softer) tail (p90 0.347, p99 0.602) and is motivated by the structural profile: heavy power-law degree (max_degree 2556, degree_std 54.82, is_power_law true) plus feature_dup_rate 0.286 create nodes whose attribute-based and structure-based rankings can diverge, a cross-modal view orthogonal to local affinity. Reconstruction is added as a global attribute+structure generative view (feature_dim 64, feature_sparsity 0.0 dense) that captures whole-neighborhood inconsistency not seen by the two local/cross-modal scorers. I deliberately drop the weak or redundant options: density is effectively dead (p50 0, p95 0.006, mean 0.005), community is flat until p99 (p90 0.217) and unreliable given clustering_coeff 0.0, and spectral/homophily_violation largely restate the neighbor-disagreement signal already covered by local_affinity.

This is a sparse (density=0.003, avg_degree=4.08), strongly homophilous (homophily=0.862) attributed graph with high-dimensional sparse bag-of-features (feature_dim=1433, feature_sparsity=0.988) and strong community structure (modularity=0.779, num_communities=97) — a citation-style network whose likely anomalies are a mix of contextual (feature perturbations against a homophilous neighborhood) and structural (injected dense subgraphs). subgraph_contrast is first because it is by far the strongest label-free deep landmarker (mean=0.405, p95=0.634, p99=0.804, and the probe note says the full run is stronger); with feature_dim>=100 its RWR-subgraph contrast plus target-reconstruction branch is the best single view for contextual/injected anomalies here. reconstruction (DOMINANT-style, feature_dim=1433) adds a global attribute+structure autoencoder view that is complementary in scope to subgraph_contrast's local view. local_affinity directly exploits the very high homophily (0.862): honest nodes agree strongly with neighbors (landmarker mean=0.827 with a heavy upper tail to p99=1.0), so agreement-breaking nodes stand out cheaply and deterministically. clique_density is included as the structural companion the three attribute-leaning views miss: feature_sparsity=0.988 and feature_dim=1433 make it applicable, and its landmarker has a sharply separated tail (mean=0.039 but p99=0.682) signalling a small population of extreme closure-weighted triangle participants consistent with injected cliques; per its design it fuses with local_affinity via per-node rank-max to span contextual + structural populations. Spectral is skipped (spectral_gap=0.0, landmarker p99=0.33, weak), and homophily_violation/attr_struct_mismatch are dropped as redundant with local_affinity/reconstruction in favour of these four complementary mechanisms.

The profile is a sparse high-dimensional citation-style graph (feature_dim=1433, feature_sparsity=0.988) with very high homophily (0.862), strong community structure (modularity=0.779, 97 communities) and no power-law degree. The landmarkers point to two distinct anomaly populations, so I compose complementary views for each. Contextual/attribute anomalies: subgraph_contrast leads because its cheap 5-epoch probe already shows a separated tail (mean 0.405, p99=0.804) and the note says the full run is much stronger; it contrasts each node against its RWR subgraph and reconstructs its features, which is exactly the mechanism high homophily (0.862) and dense features reward. reconstruction (DOMINANT/AnomalyDAE) is the canonical autoencoder companion for feature_dim=1433 and adds a global attribute+structure view distinct from the subgraph-local readout. local_affinity (mean 0.827, homophily>=0.3) gives a direct, deterministic neighbor-feature-mismatch signal that pairs with the structural view. Structural anomalies: clique_density is the standout landmarker, with an extreme upper-tail separation (p99=0.682 vs p50=0.006, mean=0.039) that is the fingerprint of injected dense subgraphs/cliques, i.e. the closure-weighted triangle population that reconstruction and contrast systematically miss; fusing it (rank-max/AOM) with local_affinity and subgraph_contrast covers contextual + structural anomalies together. Density and community landmarkers also show tails but are largely redundant with clique_density's structural coverage, and spectral is near-flat (p99=0.333, spectral_gap=0.0), so they are dropped in favour of these four complementary mechanisms.

The profile is a small, sparse, highly modular attributed graph (2708 nodes, density 0.003, modularity 0.779, homophily 0.862) with very sparse high-dim binary features (feature_dim 1433, feature_sparsity 0.988) and is_power_law false, degree_std only 5.37 with max_degree 168, all consistent with a citation-style graph carrying injected contextual + structural anomalies. subgraph_contrast is primary: its cheap 5-epoch landmarker already has the best separated upper tail (mean 0.405 -> p95 0.634 -> p99 0.804) and the note says the full run is much stronger; with feature_dim 1433 >= 100 its RWR-subgraph bilinear contrast plus target reconstruction is well suited to the contextual/injected population. clique_density is the structural companion the contrastive branch misses: it applies because feature_sparsity 0.988 >= 0.9 and feature_dim >= 100, and its landmarker shows an extreme isolated tail (p95 0.153 -> p99 0.682) that signals a few members of abnormally dense subgraphs (injected cliques) against an otherwise low-triangle background, and it fuses with local_affinity via per-node rank-max. local_affinity is justified by the strong homophily (0.862), which makes neighbor-agreement a reliable prior so that feature-perturbed nodes surface as low-affinity; it is complementary to the structural clique view. attr_struct_mismatch adds a distinct cross-modal view (attribute vs structure rank divergence, landmarker tail mean 0.182 -> p99 0.692) that catches nodes where the two modalities disagree without duplicating the neighbor-feature mechanism. Homophily_violation is dropped as redundant with local_affinity, and spectral/density are excluded for weak, unseparated tails (spectral p99 only 0.333, density p99 0.697 but no clean tail), keeping the set complementary rather than redundant.
